questions.nlq: I would like to retrieve the display names of users who have a high number of badges, together with the average score of the posts they own, and return only those users whose average post score exceeds 50, ordered by the badge count in descending order.

WITH badge_counts AS (
    SELECT "UserId" AS user_id, COUNT(*) AS badge_cnt
    FROM badges
    GROUP BY "UserId"
),
avg_scores AS (
    SELECT "OwnerUserId" AS user_id, AVG("Score") AS avg_score
    FROM posts
    GROUP BY "OwnerUserId"
)
SELECT u."DisplayName", a.avg_score
FROM users u
JOIN badge_counts b ON u."Id" = b.user_id
JOIN avg_scores a ON u."Id" = a.user_id
WHERE b.badge_cnt >= 5
  AND a.avg_score > 50
ORDER BY b.badge_cnt DESC;

meanings.gt_sql:
WITH 
-- Calculate 90th percentile reputation threshold (top 10% users)
user_percentiles AS (
    SELECT 
        Id,
        Reputation,
        NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY Reputation ASC) as percentile_group
    FROM users
    WHERE Reputation IS NOT NULL
),
prominent_user_ids AS (
    SELECT Id as UserId
    FROM user_percentiles
    WHERE percentile_group = 10
),

-- Parse tags from posts and create one row per post-tag combination
post_tags_expanded AS (
    SELECT 
        p.Id as PostId,
        p.OwnerUserId,
        TRIM(SUBSTR(
            REPLACE(REPLACE(tags_value, '<', ' '), '>', ' '),
            INSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(tags_value, '<', ' '), '>', ' '), ' ') + 1
        )) as tag_word
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            p.Id,
            p.OwnerUserId,
            p.Tags as tags_value,
            ',' || p.Tags || ',' as tags_with_commas
        FROM posts p
        WHERE p.Tags IS NOT NULL AND p.Tags != ''
    ) p,
    LATERAL (
        SELECT SUBSTR(tags_with_commas, 1, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>,') - 1) as first_tag
        UNION ALL
        SELECT SUBSTR(tags_with_commas, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>,') + 2, INSTR(SUBSTR(tags_with_commas, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>,') + 2), '>,') - 1)
    ) tags_value
),

-- Simpler tag extraction using recursive CTE for each position
post_tag_list AS (
    SELECT 
        p.Id as PostId,
        p.OwnerUserId,
        COALESCE(p.AnswerCount, 0) + COALESCE(p.FavoriteCount, 0) as popularity_score,
        SUBSTR(t.value, 2, INSTR(t.value, '>') - 2) as tag_name
    FROM posts p
    CROSS JOIN (
        WITH RECURSIVE tag_extractor(post_id, pos) AS (
            SELECT p.Id, 1 FROM posts p WHERE p.Tags IS NOT NULL AND p.Tags != ''
            UNION ALL
            SELECT post_id, pos + 1 FROM tag_extractor WHERE EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM posts WHERE Tags IS NOT NULL AND Tags != ''
            )
        )
        SELECT * FROM tag_extractor
    ) t
),

-- Calculate median popularity per tag
-- Simplified approach: calculate median using ordering
median_per_tag AS (
    SELECT 
        pt.tag_name,
        AVG(CAST(pt.popularity_score AS REAL)) as median_score
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            SUBSTR(tags_with_commas, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1) + 1, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1)) - INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1) - 1) as tag,
            p.Id as PostId,
            p.OwnerUserId,
            COALESCE(p.AnswerCount, 0) + COALESCE(p.FavoriteCount, 0) as popularity_score
        FROM posts p
        WHERE p.Tags IS NOT NULL AND p.Tags != ''
    ) pt
    GROUP BY pt.tag
),

-- Popular posts: above median for their tag
popular_posts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT p.Id as PostId, p.OwnerUserId
    FROM posts p
    CROSS JOIN (
        SELECT 
            SUBSTR(tags_with_commas, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1) + 1, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1)) - INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1) - 1) as tag,
            p.Id as PostId,
            p.OwnerUserId,
            COALESCE(p.AnswerCount, 0) + COALESCE(p.FavoriteCount, 0) as popularity_score
        FROM posts p
        WHERE p.Tags IS NOT NULL AND p.Tags != ''
    ) pc
    JOIN (
        SELECT 
            SUBSTR(tags_with_commas, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1) + 1, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1)) - INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1) - 1) as tag,
            PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY COALESCE(p2.AnswerCount, 0) + COALESCE(p2.FavoriteCount, 0)) as median_val
        FROM posts p2
        WHERE p2.Tags IS NOT NULL AND p2.Tags != ''
        GROUP BY SUBSTR(tags_with_commas, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1) + 1, INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1)) - INSTR(tags_with_commas, '>', 1) - 1)
    ) med ON TRUE
),

-- Final result: prominent users with popular posts
result AS (
    SELECT 
        u.DisplayName
    FROM users u
    JOIN prominent_user_ids piu ON u.Id = piu.UserId
    JOIN posts p ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
    JOIN popular_posts pop ON pop.PostId = p.Id
)

questions.nlq: Hey! Could you help me find recent posts that have a bunch of comments? I'd love to see the post title, the owner's display name, and how many comments each one got.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: In this context, 'recent' means posts created within the last 30 days from today.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT p.Title,
       COALESCE(p.OwnerDisplayName, u.DisplayName) AS OwnerDisplayName,
       COUNT(c.Id) AS CommentCount
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN comments c ON c.PostId = p.Id
WHERE p.CreaionDate >= datetime('now', '-30 days')
GROUP BY p.Id
HAVING COUNT(c.Id) > 0
ORDER BY CommentCount DESC;

WITH qualifying_answers AS (
    SELECT p.Id AS AnswerId, p.OwnerUserId AS UserId
    FROM posts p
    WHERE p.PostTypeId = 2
      AND p.Score > 50
      AND p.CreationDate >= datetime((SELECT MAX(CreationDate) FROM posts), '-1 month')
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM comments c
          WHERE c.PostId = p.Id AND c.Score > 60
      )
)
SELECT u.DisplayName,
       u.Reputation,
       COUNT(DISTINCT qa.AnswerId) AS answer_count,
       AVG(c.Score) AS avg_comment_score
FROM qualifying_answers qa
JOIN users u ON u.Id = qa.UserId
JOIN comments c ON c.PostId = qa.AnswerId AND c.Score > 60
GROUP BY u.Id, u.DisplayName, u.Reputation
ORDER BY answer_count DESC;

questions.nlq: Hey! Could you help me pull a list of the highly active users? I'd love to see their display name, reputation, and all the badge names they've earned. I’m not really sure where to draw the line on ‘highly active’, though.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: In this interpretation, ‘highly active’ means any user who has accumulated at least 50 total contributions, where a contribution is counted as a post they own, a comment they wrote, or a vote they cast.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH contrib AS (
    SELECT u.Id,
           u.DisplayName,
           u.Reputation,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM posts p WHERE p.OwnerUserId = u.Id) +
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c WHERE c.UserId = u.Id) +
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM votes v WHERE v.UserId = u.Id) AS total_contrib
    FROM users u
)
SELECT c.DisplayName,
       c.Reputation,
       b.Name AS BadgeName
FROM contrib c
LEFT JOIN badges b ON b.UserId = c.Id
WHERE c.total_contrib >= 50;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: In this alternative interpretation, ‘highly active’ means any user whose total contribution count is in the top 5 % of all users (based on the combined number of posts, comments, and votes).
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH user_contrib AS (
    SELECT u.Id,
           u.DisplayName,
           u.Reputation,
           COALESCE(p.post_cnt, 0) + COALESCE(c.comment_cnt, 0) + COALESCE(v.vote_cnt, 0) AS total_contrib
    FROM users u
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT OwnerUserId AS user_id, COUNT(*) AS post_cnt
        FROM posts
        GROUP BY OwnerUserId
    ) p ON u.Id = p.user_id
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT UserId AS user_id, COUNT(*) AS comment_cnt
        FROM comments
        GROUP BY UserId
    ) c ON u.Id = c.user_id
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT UserId AS user_id, COUNT(*) AS vote_cnt
        FROM votes
        GROUP BY UserId
    ) v ON u.Id = v.user_id
),
top_n AS (
    SELECT MAX(1, CAST(cnt * 0.05 AS INTEGER)) AS n
    FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM users)
),
threshold AS (
    SELECT MIN(total_contrib) AS min_total
    FROM (
        SELECT total_contrib
        FROM user_contrib
        ORDER BY total_contrib DESC
        LIMIT (SELECT n FROM top_n)
    )
)
SELECT uc.DisplayName,
       uc.Reputation,
       b.Name AS BadgeName
FROM user_contrib uc
CROSS JOIN threshold t
LEFT JOIN badges b ON b.UserId = uc.Id
WHERE uc.total_contrib >= t.min_total
ORDER BY uc.total_contrib DESC, b.Name;

    SELECT Score AS perc_score
    FROM (
        SELECT Score,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Score) AS rn

    WHERE rn = CEIL(cnt * 0.75)
)
SELECT Id
FROM posts
WHERE Score > (SELECT perc_score FROM perc);

SELECT p.Id, p.Title
FROM posts AS p
JOIN (
    SELECT PostId, COUNT(*) AS recent_votes
    FROM votes
    WHERE CreationDate >= datetime('now','-30 day')
    GROUP BY PostId
) AS v ON p.Id = v.PostId
ORDER BY v.recent_votes DESC;
